messages:
maya: Heads-up: int8 canary (raven-lite-q4a) shows elevated funcall parse fails on streaming (+1.9% window).
oliver: Any sign it's tokenization vs truncation?
sam: Truncation. Stream flush cuts mid-json array suffix. sample log:
```
...\"actions\":[{\"name\":\"lookup\",\"args\":{...}},
<STREAM_CUTOFF>
```
maya: non-streaming paths fine -> likely streaming batching/ratecap interaction
sophia: possible burst flush aligns with array suffix. two quick mitigations: sentinel terminator or smart flush on suffix patterns
oliver: sentinel fastest. add '<JSON_TERM>' to end of prompt and strip client-side before parse
maya: ran sentinel canary (~20k req): parse fails 3.2% -> 0.6%, tokens +0.8%
sam: alternative: reduce batch_max_tokens by 20% for streaming funcall routes; should reduce mid-object flushes with lower cost
oliver: run parallel canaries sentinel vs reduced-batch and collect funcall_parse_fail, p99-token-loss, token_delta, cpu_alloc
deploy-bot: deployed: canary/stream-sentinel-probe v0.1 -> canary cluster
sam: results uploaded s3://redwood-canaries/1748888888/results.json
maya: summary: sentinel best reliability but cost bump; reduced-batch reduces failures and cost moderately. next step: prototype runtime flush (pattern-detect) and perf bench
oliver: filing follow-up phab ticket T12345 to track runtime change
sophia: also add monitor alert if funcall parse delta >0.5% baseline
maya: noted, adding to canary playbook and retro agenda :white_check_mark:
